title: Steam Gives You 48 Hours. Most Indie Devs Waste All of Them.
description:
Most indie devs think a Steam launch is something you execute on Day 1. It's not. It's something you mostly decide weeks before, in fields you click through in Steamworks without thinking. In this episode of Indie Growth Clinic, we break down the 5 mistakes that quietly kill your launch window, often before you ever hit publish.

We'll walk through how Steam's algorithm actually reads your first 48 hours, why the wishlist email you trust is the one most likely to fail you, and how a single field change in Steamworks can erase free front-page visibility you'll never get back. Then we'll hand you a 5-point launch checklist you can run before you commit to a date.

If you're a solo dev or small studio shipping on Steam this year, this one's for you.

─────────────────────────────
🎮 GET MORE EYES ON YOUR STEAM PAGE
Register your game on QUDO and put it in front of a community that actively plays, comments, and wishlists indie games. Real playtime feeds Steam's algorithm in your launch window. Comments and reviews give new visitors social proof. Both start with your game being seen.
→ http://games.qudo.io/?utm_source=Youtube&utm_medium=longform&utm_campaign=qudo_indie_channel&utm_content=Growth%20Clinic%20Steam%20Gives%20You%2048%20Hours

─────────────────────────────
📌 WHAT'S COVERED IN THIS VIDEO
00:00 – The 130,000 wishlists that never got an email
00:28 – How the Steam launch window actually works
03:05 – Mistake 1: Burning the wishlist email before launch
06:28 – Mistake 2: No coordinated traffic on Day 1
08:05 – Mistake 3: Going dark after Day 1
09:13 – Mistake 4: Setting and moving your release date
10:09 – Mistake 5: Launching into a Steam sale
11:36 – The 48-Hour Launch Window Checklist
13:49 – How to use QUDO to feed your launch signals

─────────────────────────────
🌐 SOURCES
https://newsletter.gamediscover.co/p/how-your-steam-launch-players-relate by Simon Carless (GameDiscoverCo) — New & Trending mechanics + Week 1 CCU multiplier
https://presskit.gg/blog/how-steam-wishlists-work — wishlist email triggers, deliverability, 2-week cooldown
https://www.pcgamer.com/games/survival-crafting/9-months-after-its-1-0-launch-flopped-an-indie-dev-just-learned-that-steam-never-emailed-the-130-000-people-who-wishlisted-its-game/ — Planet Centauri 130,000 wishlist email failure
https://gameifyouare.com/2022/12/15/how-many-steam-wishlists-does-my-indie-game-need/ — wishlist thresholds for Popular Upcoming
https://www.game-oracle.com/blog/best-time-to-release — Steam sale timing
https://www.valadria.com/steam-dev-cheat-sheet/ — Steam dev cheat sheet
https://steamdb.info/sales/ — Steam sales calendar

─────────────────────────────
💬 DROP YOUR ANSWER IN THE COMMENTS
Which of the 5 mistakes did you recognize in your own launch plans, or already make? Burning the wishlist email, no coordinated Day 1 traffic, going dark on Day 2, moving your release date, or launching into a sale?
We read every comment, and the pattern of answers shapes what we go deep on next.

─────────────────────────────
📺 MORE FROM INDIE GROWTH CLINIC
This series covers onboarding, first session, retention, community loops, marketing hooks, store pages, and launch planning. All through real case studies, not theory.

Subscribe so you don't miss the next breakdown.
